Repeated integration by parts reduces polynomial factors against exponentials or trigonometric
functions. Sometimes the original integral reappears, producing an algebraic equation to solve.
Boundary terms matter, especially in definite and improper integrals; evaluate their limits
rather than dropping them. Differentiation is a quick verification of an indefinite result.
